# Function list

<!-- Generated by `cargo xtask site` from crates/kiln-formula/docs/. Do not edit by hand. -->

Kiln Grid has 505 worksheet functions, spelled as Excel spells them. **Formulas ▸ Insert Function** searches this list and shows each function's arguments and examples. See [Formulas in Kiln Grid](grid-formulas.md).

## Compatibility

| Function | What it does |
|---|---|
| `BETADIST(x, alpha, beta, [A], [B])` | Returns the cumulative beta distribution. Use BETA.DIST in new workbooks. |
| `BETAINV(probability, alpha, beta, [A], [B])` | Returns the inverse of the cumulative beta distribution. Use BETA.INV in new workbooks. |
| `BINOMDIST(number_s, trials, probability_s, cumulative)` | Returns the binomial distribution probability. Use BINOM.DIST in new workbooks. |
| `CEILING(number, significance)` | Rounds a number up (away from zero for negative significance) to the nearest multiple of significance. |
| `CHIDIST(x, deg_freedom)` | Returns the right-tailed probability of the chi-squared distribution. Use CHISQ.DIST.RT in new workbooks. |
| `CHIINV(probability, deg_freedom)` | Returns the inverse of the right-tailed chi-squared distribution. Use CHISQ.INV.RT in new workbooks. |
| `CHITEST(actual_range, expected_range)` | Returns the test for independence. Use CHISQ.TEST in new workbooks. |
| `CONFIDENCE(alpha, standard_dev, size)` | Returns the confidence interval for a population mean. Use CONFIDENCE.NORM in new workbooks. |
| `COVAR(array1, array2)` | Returns covariance, the average of the products of paired deviations. Use COVARIANCE.P in new workbooks. |
| `CRITBINOM(trials, probability_s, alpha)` | Returns the smallest value for which the cumulative binomial distribution is at least the criterion. Use BINOM.INV in new workbooks. |
| `EXPONDIST(x, lambda, cumulative)` | Returns the exponential distribution. Use EXPON.DIST in new workbooks. |
| `FDIST(x, deg_freedom1, deg_freedom2)` | Returns the right-tailed F probability distribution. Use F.DIST.RT in new workbooks. |
| `FINV(probability, deg_freedom1, deg_freedom2)` | Returns the inverse of the right-tailed F distribution. Use F.INV.RT in new workbooks. |
| `FLOOR(number, significance)` | Rounds a number down, toward zero, to the nearest multiple of significance. |
| `FORECAST(x, known_y's, known_x's)` | Predicts a value along a linear trend. Use FORECAST.LINEAR in new workbooks. |
| `FTEST(array1, array2)` | Returns the result of an F-test. Use F.TEST in new workbooks. |
| `GAMMADIST(x, alpha, beta, cumulative)` | Returns the gamma distribution. Use GAMMA.DIST in new workbooks. |
| `GAMMAINV(probability, alpha, beta)` | Returns the inverse of the gamma cumulative distribution. Use GAMMA.INV in new workbooks. |
| `HYPGEOMDIST(sample_s, number_sample, population_s, number_pop)` | Returns the hypergeometric probability. Use HYPGEOM.DIST in new workbooks. |
| `LOGINV(probability, mean, standard_dev)` | Returns the inverse of the lognormal cumulative distribution. Use LOGNORM.INV in new workbooks. |
| `LOGNORMDIST(x, mean, standard_dev)` | Returns the cumulative lognormal distribution. Use LOGNORM.DIST in new workbooks. |
| `MODE(number1, [number2], ...)` | Returns the most common value in a data set. Use MODE.SNGL in new workbooks. |
| `NEGBINOMDIST(number_f, number_s, probability_s)` | Returns the negative binomial distribution. Use NEGBINOM.DIST in new workbooks. |
| `NORMDIST(x, mean, standard_dev, cumulative)` | Returns the normal distribution. Use NORM.DIST in new workbooks. |
| `NORMINV(probability, mean, standard_dev)` | Returns the inverse of the normal cumulative distribution. Use NORM.INV in new workbooks. |
| `NORMSDIST(z)` | Returns the standard normal cumulative distribution. Use NORM.S.DIST in new workbooks. |
| `NORMSINV(probability)` | Returns the inverse of the standard normal cumulative distribution. Use NORM.S.INV in new workbooks. |
| `PERCENTILE(array, k)` | Returns the k-th percentile of values. Use PERCENTILE.INC in new workbooks. |
| `PERCENTRANK(array, x, [significance])` | Returns the percentage rank of a value in a data set. Use PERCENTRANK.INC in new workbooks. |
| `POISSON(x, mean, cumulative)` | Returns the Poisson distribution. Use POISSON.DIST in new workbooks. |
| `QUARTILE(array, quart)` | Returns the quartile of a data set. Use QUARTILE.INC in new workbooks. |
| `RANK(number, ref, [order])` | Returns the rank of a number in a list. Use RANK.EQ in new workbooks. |
| `STDEV(number1, [number2], ...)` | Estimates standard deviation based on a sample. Use STDEV.S in new workbooks. |
| `STDEVP(number1, [number2], ...)` | Calculates standard deviation of an entire population. Use STDEV.P in new workbooks. |
| `TDIST(x, deg_freedom, tails)` | Returns the Student's t-distribution. Use T.DIST.RT or T.DIST.2T in new workbooks. |
| `TINV(probability, deg_freedom)` | Returns the two-tailed inverse of the Student's t-distribution. Use T.INV.2T in new workbooks. |
| `TTEST(array1, array2, tails, type)` | Returns the probability associated with a Student's t-test. Use T.TEST in new workbooks. |
| `VAR(number1, [number2], ...)` | Estimates variance based on a sample. Use VAR.S in new workbooks. |
| `VARP(number1, [number2], ...)` | Calculates variance of an entire population. Use VAR.P in new workbooks. |
| `WEIBULL(x, alpha, beta, cumulative)` | Returns the Weibull distribution. Use WEIBULL.DIST in new workbooks. |
| `ZTEST(array, x, [sigma])` | Returns the one-tailed probability-value of a z-test. Use Z.TEST in new workbooks. |

## Database

| Function | What it does |
|---|---|
| `DAVERAGE(database, field, criteria)` | Averages the values in a database column that match conditions. |
| `DCOUNT(database, [field], criteria)` | Counts the numeric cells in a database column that match conditions. |
| `DCOUNTA(database, field, criteria)` | Counts the non-empty cells in a database column that match conditions. |
| `DGET(database, field, criteria)` | Extracts the single value from a database column that matches conditions. |
| `DMAX(database, field, criteria)` | Returns the largest value in a database column that matches conditions. |
| `DMIN(database, field, criteria)` | Returns the smallest value in a database column that matches conditions. |
| `DPRODUCT(database, field, criteria)` | Multiplies the values in a database column that match conditions. |
| `DSTDEV(database, field, criteria)` | Estimates the standard deviation of a sample from a database column that matches conditions. |
| `DSTDEVP(database, field, criteria)` | Calculates the population standard deviation of a database column that matches conditions. |
| `DSUM(database, field, criteria)` | Adds the values in a database column that match conditions. |
| `DVAR(database, field, criteria)` | Estimates the variance of a sample from a database column that matches conditions. |
| `DVARP(database, field, criteria)` | Calculates the population variance of a database column that matches conditions. |

## Date & Time

| Function | What it does |
|---|---|
| `DATE(year, month, day)` | Returns the serial number of a date; months and days may overflow (month 13 is January next year). |
| `DATEDIF(start_date, end_date, unit)` | Calculates the number of days, months or years between two dates. |
| `DATEVALUE(date_text)` | Converts a date written as text to a serial number. |
| `DAY(serial_number)` | Returns the day of the month (1–31) of a date. |
| `DAYS(end_date, start_date)` | Returns the number of days between two dates. |
| `DAYS360(start_date, end_date, [method])` | Returns the number of days between two dates based on a 360-day year. |
| `EDATE(start_date, months)` | Returns the date a number of months before or after a start date. |
| `EOMONTH(start_date, months)` | Returns the last day of the month a number of months before or after a start date. |
| `HOUR(serial_number)` | Returns the hour (0–23) of a time value. |
| `ISOWEEKNUM(date)` | Returns the ISO week number of the year for a date. |
| `MINUTE(serial_number)` | Returns the minute (0–59) of a time value. |
| `MONTH(serial_number)` | Returns the month (1–12) of a date. |
| `NETWORKDAYS(start_date, end_date, [holidays])` | Returns the number of whole working days between two dates (Monday to Friday, minus holidays). |
| `NETWORKDAYS.INTL(start_date, end_date, [weekend], [holidays])` | Returns the number of whole working days between two dates with custom weekends. |
| `NOW()` | Returns the current date and time as a serial number. |
| `SECOND(serial_number)` | Returns the second (0–59) of a time value. |
| `TIME(hour, minute, second)` | Returns the serial number of a time. |
| `TIMEVALUE(time_text)` | Converts a time written as text to a serial number. |
| `TODAY()` | Returns today's date as a serial number. |
| `WEEKDAY(serial_number, [return_type])` | Returns the day of the week for a date. |
| `WEEKNUM(serial_number, [return_type])` | Returns the week number of a date in the year. |
| `WORKDAY(start_date, days, [holidays])` | Returns the date a number of working days before or after a start date. |
| `WORKDAY.INTL(start_date, days, [weekend], [holidays])` | Returns the date a number of working days away, with custom weekends. |
| `YEAR(serial_number)` | Returns the year of a date. |
| `YEARFRAC(start_date, end_date, [basis])` | Returns the fraction of the year between two dates. |

## Engineering

| Function | What it does |
|---|---|
| `BESSELI(x, n)` | Returns the modified Bessel function In(x). |
| `BESSELJ(x, n)` | Returns the Bessel function Jn(x). |
| `BESSELK(x, n)` | Returns the modified Bessel function Kn(x). |
| `BESSELY(x, n)` | Returns the Bessel function Yn(x), also called the Weber or Neumann function. |
| `BIN2DEC(number)` | Converts a binary number to decimal. |
| `BIN2HEX(number, [places])` | Converts a binary number to hexadecimal. |
| `BIN2OCT(number, [places])` | Converts a binary number to octal. |
| `BITAND(number1, number2)` | Returns a bitwise AND of two numbers. |
| `BITLSHIFT(number, shift_amount)` | Returns a number shifted left by the given number of bits. |
| `BITOR(number1, number2)` | Returns a bitwise OR of two numbers. |
| `BITRSHIFT(number, shift_amount)` | Returns a number shifted right by the given number of bits. |
| `BITXOR(number1, number2)` | Returns a bitwise exclusive OR of two numbers. |
| `COMPLEX(real_num, i_num, [suffix])` | Converts real and imaginary coefficients into a complex number. |
| `CONVERT(number, from_unit, to_unit)` | Converts a number from one measurement system to another. |
| `DEC2BIN(number, [places])` | Converts a decimal number to binary. |
| `DEC2HEX(number, [places])` | Converts a decimal number to hexadecimal. |
| `DEC2OCT(number, [places])` | Converts a decimal number to octal. |
| `DELTA(number1, [number2])` | Tests whether two values are equal (1) or not (0). |
| `ERF(lower_limit, [upper_limit])` | Returns the error function integrated between lower_limit and upper_limit (or 0 and lower_limit). |
| `ERF.PRECISE(x)` | Returns the error function. |
| `ERFC(x)` | Returns the complementary error function. |
| `ERFC.PRECISE(x)` | Returns the complementary error function. |
| `GESTEP(number, [step])` | Returns 1 if a number is greater than or equal to a threshold, otherwise 0. |
| `HEX2BIN(number, [places])` | Converts a hexadecimal number to binary. |
| `HEX2DEC(number)` | Converts a hexadecimal number to decimal. |
| `HEX2OCT(number, [places])` | Converts a hexadecimal number to octal. |
| `IMABS(inumber)` | Returns the absolute value (modulus) of a complex number. |
| `IMAGINARY(inumber)` | Returns the imaginary coefficient of a complex number. |
| `IMARGUMENT(inumber)` | Returns the argument theta, an angle in radians. |
| `IMCONJUGATE(inumber)` | Returns the complex conjugate of a complex number. |
| `IMCOS(inumber)` | Returns the cosine of a complex number. |
| `IMCOSH(inumber)` | Returns the hyperbolic cosine of a complex number. |
| `IMCOT(inumber)` | Returns the cotangent of a complex number. |
| `IMCSC(inumber)` | Returns the cosecant of a complex number. |
| `IMCSCH(inumber)` | Returns the hyperbolic cosecant of a complex number. |
| `IMDIV(inumber1, inumber2)` | Returns the quotient of two complex numbers. |
| `IMEXP(inumber)` | Returns the exponential of a complex number. |
| `IMLN(inumber)` | Returns the natural logarithm of a complex number. |
| `IMLOG10(inumber)` | Returns the base-10 logarithm of a complex number. |
| `IMLOG2(inumber)` | Returns the base-2 logarithm of a complex number. |
| `IMPOWER(inumber, number)` | Returns a complex number raised to a power. |
| `IMPRODUCT(inumber1, [inumber2], ...)` | Returns the product of complex numbers. |
| `IMREAL(inumber)` | Returns the real coefficient of a complex number. |
| `IMSEC(inumber)` | Returns the secant of a complex number. |
| `IMSECH(inumber)` | Returns the hyperbolic secant of a complex number. |
| `IMSIN(inumber)` | Returns the sine of a complex number. |
| `IMSINH(inumber)` | Returns the hyperbolic sine of a complex number. |
| `IMSQRT(inumber)` | Returns the square root of a complex number. |
| `IMSUB(inumber1, inumber2)` | Returns the difference of two complex numbers. |
| `IMSUM(inumber1, [inumber2], ...)` | Returns the sum of complex numbers. |
| `IMTAN(inumber)` | Returns the tangent of a complex number. |
| `OCT2BIN(number, [places])` | Converts an octal number to binary. |
| `OCT2DEC(number)` | Converts an octal number to decimal. |
| `OCT2HEX(number, [places])` | Converts an octal number to hexadecimal. |

## Financial

| Function | What it does |
|---|---|
| `ACCRINT(issue, first_interest, settlement, rate, par, frequency, [basis], [calc_method])` | Returns the accrued interest for a security that pays periodic interest. |
| `ACCRINTM(issue, settlement, rate, [par], [basis])` | Returns the accrued interest for a security that pays interest at maturity. |
| `AMORDEGRC(cost, date_purchased, first_period, salvage, period, rate, [basis])` | Returns the depreciation for each accounting period in the French accounting system, with a depreciation coefficient that depends on the asset's life. |
| `AMORLINC(cost, date_purchased, first_period, salvage, period, rate, [basis])` | Returns the straight-line depreciation for each accounting period in the French accounting system, prorating the first period. |
| `COUPDAYBS(settlement, maturity, frequency, [basis])` | Returns the number of days from the beginning of the coupon period to the settlement date. |
| `COUPDAYS(settlement, maturity, frequency, [basis])` | Returns the number of days in the coupon period that contains the settlement date. |
| `COUPDAYSNC(settlement, maturity, frequency, [basis])` | Returns the number of days from the settlement date to the next coupon date. |
| `COUPNCD(settlement, maturity, frequency, [basis])` | Returns the next coupon date after the settlement date. |
| `COUPNUM(settlement, maturity, frequency, [basis])` | Returns the number of coupons payable between the settlement date and maturity date. |
| `COUPPCD(settlement, maturity, frequency, [basis])` | Returns the previous coupon date before the settlement date. |
| `CUMIPMT(rate, nper, pv, start_period, end_period, type)` | Returns the cumulative interest paid on a loan between two periods. |
| `CUMPRINC(rate, nper, pv, start_period, end_period, type)` | Returns the cumulative principal paid on a loan between two periods. |
| `DB(cost, salvage, life, period, [month])` | Returns the depreciation of an asset for a period using the fixed-declining balance method. |
| `DDB(cost, salvage, life, period, [factor])` | Returns the depreciation of an asset for a period using the double-declining balance (or another) method. |
| `DISC(settlement, maturity, pr, redemption, [basis])` | Returns the discount rate for a security. |
| `DOLLARDE(fractional_dollar, fraction)` | Converts a dollar price expressed as a fraction into a decimal number. |
| `DOLLARFR(decimal_dollar, fraction)` | Converts a decimal dollar price into a fractional price. |
| `DURATION(settlement, maturity, coupon, yld, frequency, [basis])` | Returns the Macaulay duration of a security with periodic interest payments. |
| `EFFECT(nominal_rate, npery)` | Returns the effective annual interest rate. |
| `EUROCONVERT(number, source, target, [full_precision], [triangulation_precision])` | Converts a number to euros, from euros to a euro member currency, or between two member currencies through the euro (triangulation), at the fixed conversion rates. |
| `FV(rate, nper, pmt, [pv], [type])` | Returns the future value of an investment with periodic, constant payments and a constant rate. |
| `FVSCHEDULE(principal, schedule)` | Returns the future value of a principal after applying a series of compound interest rates. |
| `INTRATE(settlement, maturity, investment, redemption, [basis])` | Returns the interest rate for a fully invested security. |
| `IPMT(rate, per, nper, pv, [fv], [type])` | Returns the interest payment for a given period of an investment. |
| `IRR(values, [guess])` | Returns the internal rate of return for a series of cash flows. |
| `ISPMT(rate, per, nper, pv)` | Returns the interest paid during a period of a loan with even principal payments. |
| `MDURATION(settlement, maturity, coupon, yld, frequency, [basis])` | Returns the modified Macaulay duration of a security. |
| `MIRR(values, finance_rate, reinvest_rate)` | Returns the modified internal rate of return for a series of cash flows. |
| `NOMINAL(effect_rate, npery)` | Returns the annual nominal interest rate. |
| `NPER(rate, pmt, pv, [fv], [type])` | Returns the number of periods for an investment. |
| `NPV(rate, value1, [value2], ...)` | Returns the net present value of an investment from a discount rate and future cash flows. |
| `ODDFPRICE(settlement, maturity, issue, first_coupon, rate, yld, redemption, frequency, [basis])` | Returns the price per $100 face value of a security with an odd (short or long) first period. |
| `ODDFYIELD(settlement, maturity, issue, first_coupon, rate, pr, redemption, frequency, [basis])` | Returns the yield of a security with an odd (short or long) first period. |
| `ODDLPRICE(settlement, maturity, last_interest, rate, yld, redemption, frequency, [basis])` | Returns the price per $100 face value of a security with an odd last period. |
| `ODDLYIELD(settlement, maturity, last_interest, rate, pr, redemption, frequency, [basis])` | Returns the yield of a security with an odd last period. |
| `PDURATION(rate, pv, fv)` | Returns the number of periods required for an investment to reach a value. |
| `PMT(rate, nper, pv, [fv], [type])` | Returns the periodic payment for a loan. |
| `PPMT(rate, per, nper, pv, [fv], [type])` | Returns the principal payment for a given period of an investment. |
| `PRICE(settlement, maturity, rate, yld, redemption, frequency, [basis])` | Returns the price per $100 face value of a security that pays periodic interest. |
| `PRICEDISC(settlement, maturity, discount, redemption, [basis])` | Returns the price per $100 face value of a discounted security. |
| `PRICEMAT(settlement, maturity, issue, rate, yld, [basis])` | Returns the price per $100 face value of a security that pays interest at maturity. |
| `PV(rate, nper, pmt, [fv], [type])` | Returns the present value of an investment. |
| `RATE(nper, pmt, pv, [fv], [type], [guess])` | Returns the interest rate per period of an annuity. |
| `RECEIVED(settlement, maturity, investment, discount, [basis])` | Returns the amount received at maturity for a fully invested security. |
| `RRI(nper, pv, fv)` | Returns an equivalent interest rate for the growth of an investment. |
| `SLN(cost, salvage, life)` | Returns the straight-line depreciation of an asset for one period. |
| `SYD(cost, salvage, life, per)` | Returns the sum-of-years' digits depreciation of an asset for a period. |
| `TBILLEQ(settlement, maturity, discount)` | Returns the bond-equivalent yield for a Treasury bill. |
| `TBILLPRICE(settlement, maturity, discount)` | Returns the price per $100 face value for a Treasury bill. |
| `TBILLYIELD(settlement, maturity, pr)` | Returns the yield for a Treasury bill. |
| `VDB(cost, salvage, life, start_period, end_period, [factor], [no_switch])` | Returns the depreciation of an asset for any period, using the declining balance method and switching to straight line. |
| `XIRR(values, dates, [guess])` | Returns the internal rate of return for a schedule of cash flows that is not necessarily periodic. |
| `XNPV(rate, values, dates)` | Returns the net present value for a schedule of cash flows that is not necessarily periodic. |
| `YIELD(settlement, maturity, rate, pr, redemption, frequency, [basis])` | Returns the yield of a security that pays periodic interest. |
| `YIELDDISC(settlement, maturity, pr, redemption, [basis])` | Returns the annual yield for a discounted security. |
| `YIELDMAT(settlement, maturity, issue, rate, pr, [basis])` | Returns the annual yield of a security that pays interest at maturity. |

## Information

| Function | What it does |
|---|---|
| `CELL(info_type, [reference])` | Returns information about the formatting, location or contents of a cell (address, col, row, contents, type, filename). |
| `ERROR.TYPE(error_val)` | Returns a number for an error value (1 #NULL!, 2 #DIV/0!, 3 #VALUE!, 4 #REF!, 5 #NAME?, 6 #NUM!, 7 #N/A …). |
| `INFO(type_text)` | Returns information about the operating environment (numfile, recalc, release, system, osversion, origin). |
| `ISBLANK(value)` | Returns TRUE if the value is an empty cell. |
| `ISERR(value)` | Returns TRUE if the value is any error except #N/A. |
| `ISERROR(value)` | Returns TRUE if the value is any error. |
| `ISEVEN(number)` | Returns TRUE if the number is even. |
| `ISFORMULA(reference)` | Returns TRUE if the cell contains a formula. |
| `ISLOGICAL(value)` | Returns TRUE if the value is a logical value. |
| `ISNA(value)` | Returns TRUE if the value is the #N/A error. |
| `ISNONTEXT(value)` | Returns TRUE if the value is not text. |
| `ISNUMBER(value)` | Returns TRUE if the value is a number. |
| `ISODD(number)` | Returns TRUE if the number is odd. |
| `ISREF(value)` | Returns TRUE if the value is a reference. |
| `ISTEXT(value)` | Returns TRUE if the value is text. |
| `N(value)` | Returns a value converted to a number (text becomes 0, TRUE 1). |
| `NA()` | Returns the error value #N/A. |
| `SHEET([value])` | Returns the sheet number of a reference or sheet name. |
| `SHEETS([reference])` | Returns the number of sheets in a reference (or in the workbook). |
| `TYPE(value)` | Returns a number for the data type of a value (1 number, 2 text, 4 logical, 16 error, 64 array, 128 lambda). |

## Logical

| Function | What it does |
|---|---|
| `AND(logical1, [logical2], ...)` | Returns TRUE if all of its arguments are TRUE. |
| `BYCOL(array, lambda)` | Applies a LAMBDA to each column and returns an array of the results. |
| `BYROW(array, lambda)` | Applies a LAMBDA to each row and returns an array of the results. |
| `FALSE()` | Returns the logical value FALSE. |
| `IF(logical_test, value_if_true, [value_if_false])` | Returns one value if a condition is TRUE and another if it is FALSE. |
| `IFERROR(value, value_if_error)` | Returns a value you specify if a formula evaluates to an error; otherwise the formula result. |
| `IFNA(value, value_if_na)` | Returns a value you specify if a formula returns #N/A; otherwise the formula result. |
| `IFS(logical_test1, value_if_true1, [logical_test2, value_if_true2], ...)` | Returns the value for the first condition that is TRUE. |
| `ISOMITTED(argument)` | Checks whether a LAMBDA argument was omitted. |
| `LAMBDA([parameter], ..., calculation)` | Creates a reusable function with parameters. |
| `LET(name1, value1, [name2, value2], ..., calculation)` | Assigns names to calculation results so they can be reused in a formula. |
| `MAKEARRAY(rows, columns, lambda)` | Returns an array of the given size whose values are calculated by a LAMBDA. |
| `MAP(array1, [array2], ..., lambda)` | Returns an array formed by applying a LAMBDA to each value of the arrays. |
| `NOT(logical)` | Reverses a logical value. |
| `OR(logical1, [logical2], ...)` | Returns TRUE if any argument is TRUE. |
| `REDUCE([initial_value], array, lambda)` | Reduces an array to an accumulated value by applying a LAMBDA to each value. |
| `SCAN([initial_value], array, lambda)` | Scans an array by applying a LAMBDA to each value, returning every intermediate value. |
| `SWITCH(expression, value1, result1, [default_or_value2, result2], ...)` | Compares a value with a list of values and returns the result for the first match. |
| `TRUE()` | Returns the logical value TRUE. |
| `XOR(logical1, [logical2], ...)` | Returns TRUE when an odd number of arguments are TRUE. |

## Lookup & Reference

| Function | What it does |
|---|---|
| `ADDRESS(row_num, column_num, [abs_num], [a1], [sheet_text])` | Returns a cell address as text from row and column numbers. |
| `AREAS(reference)` | Returns the number of areas in a reference. |
| `CHOOSE(index_num, value1, [value2], ...)` | Chooses a value from a list by index. |
| `CHOOSECOLS(array, col_num1, [col_num2], ...)` | Returns the specified columns of an array. |
| `CHOOSEROWS(array, row_num1, [row_num2], ...)` | Returns the specified rows of an array. |
| `COLUMN([reference])` | Returns the column number of a reference (or of the formula cell). |
| `COLUMNS(array)` | Returns the number of columns in a reference or array. |
| `DROP(array, rows, [columns])` | Drops rows or columns from the start or end of an array. |
| `EXPAND(array, rows, [columns], [pad_with])` | Expands an array to the given rows and columns, padding with a value. |
| `FILTER(array, include, [if_empty])` | Filters a range or array by a condition. |
| `FORMULATEXT(reference)` | Returns the formula of a cell as text. |
| `GETPIVOTDATA(data_field, pivot_table, [field1, item1], ...)` | Returns a value of a PivotTable report by its value field and the items of its row and column fields. |
| `GROUPBY(row_fields, values, function, [field_headers], [total_depth], [sort_order], [filter_array], [field_relationship])` | Groups rows by the values of one or more fields and aggregates the values of each group. |
| `HLOOKUP(lookup_value, table_array, row_index_num, [range_lookup])` | Looks for a value in the top row of a table and returns a value from the same column. |
| `HSTACK(array1, [array2], ...)` | Appends arrays horizontally. |
| `HYPERLINK(link_location, [friendly_name])` | Creates a link: the cell shows the friendly name and opens the link when clicked. |
| `INDEX(array, row_num, [column_num], [area_num])` | Returns the value or reference at a row and column of a range or array. |
| `INDIRECT(ref_text, [a1])` | Returns the reference named by a text string. |
| `LOOKUP(lookup_value, lookup_vector, [result_vector])` | Looks up a value in a sorted row or column (or the first row/column of an array) and returns the matching value. |
| `MATCH(lookup_value, lookup_array, [match_type])` | Returns the relative position of a value in a row or column. |
| `OFFSET(reference, rows, cols, [height], [width])` | Returns a reference offset from a starting reference by rows and columns. |
| `PIVOTBY(row_fields, col_fields, values, function, [field_headers], [row_total_depth], [row_sort_order], [col_total_depth], [col_sort_order], [filter_array], [relative_to])` | Summarises values by row fields down and column fields across, with totals. |
| `ROW([reference])` | Returns the row number of a reference (or of the formula cell). |
| `ROWS(array)` | Returns the number of rows in a reference or array. |
| `SORT(array, [sort_index], [sort_order], [by_col])` | Sorts the contents of a range or array. |
| `SORTBY(array, by_array1, [sort_order1], [by_array2, sort_order2], ...)` | Sorts a range or array by the values in corresponding ranges or arrays. |
| `TAKE(array, rows, [columns])` | Returns rows or columns from the start or end of an array. |
| `TOCOL(array, [ignore], [scan_by_column])` | Returns the array as one column. |
| `TOROW(array, [ignore], [scan_by_column])` | Returns the array as one row. |
| `TRANSPOSE(array)` | Swaps the rows and columns of a range or array. |
| `TRIMRANGE(range, [trim_rows], [trim_cols])` | Returns a range without its empty leading and trailing rows and columns. |
| `UNIQUE(array, [by_col], [exactly_once])` | Returns the unique rows (or columns) of a range or array. |
| `VLOOKUP(lookup_value, table_array, col_index_num, [range_lookup])` | Looks for a value in the first column of a table and returns a value from the same row. |
| `VSTACK(array1, [array2], ...)` | Appends arrays vertically. |
| `WRAPCOLS(vector, wrap_count, [pad_with])` | Wraps a row or column of values into columns of the given height. |
| `WRAPROWS(vector, wrap_count, [pad_with])` | Wraps a row or column of values into rows of the given width. |
| `XLOOKUP(lookup_value, lookup_array, return_array, [if_not_found], [match_mode], [search_mode])` | Searches a range or array and returns the matching item from another range or array. |
| `XMATCH(lookup_value, lookup_array, [match_mode], [search_mode])` | Returns the relative position of an item in a row or column. |

## Math & Trig

| Function | What it does |
|---|---|
| `ABS(number)` | Returns the absolute value of a number. |
| `ACOS(number)` | Returns the arccosine of a number, in radians (0 to pi). |
| `ACOSH(number)` | Returns the inverse hyperbolic cosine of a number. |
| `ACOT(number)` | Returns the principal value of the arccotangent of a number, in radians (0 to pi). |
| `ACOTH(number)` | Returns the inverse hyperbolic cotangent of a number. |
| `AGGREGATE(function_num, options, ref1, [ref2], ...)` | Returns an aggregate (sum, average, count, large…) of a list, optionally ignoring hidden rows, errors and nested SUBTOTAL/AGGREGATE results. |
| `ARABIC(text)` | Converts a Roman numeral to an Arabic number. |
| `ASIN(number)` | Returns the arcsine of a number, in radians (-pi/2 to pi/2). |
| `ASINH(number)` | Returns the inverse hyperbolic sine of a number. |
| `ATAN(number)` | Returns the arctangent of a number, in radians (-pi/2 to pi/2). |
| `ATAN2(x_num, y_num)` | Returns the arctangent of x- and y-coordinates, in radians (-pi to pi). |
| `ATANH(number)` | Returns the inverse hyperbolic tangent of a number. |
| `BASE(number, radix, [min_length])` | Converts a number into a text representation in another base (radix). |
| `CEILING.MATH(number, [significance], [mode])` | Rounds a number up to the nearest integer or multiple of significance. |
| `CEILING.PRECISE(number, [significance])` | Rounds a number up to the nearest multiple of significance, regardless of sign. |
| `COMBIN(number, number_chosen)` | Returns the number of combinations for a given number of items. |
| `COMBINA(number, number_chosen)` | Returns the number of combinations (with repetitions) for a given number of items. |
| `COS(number)` | Returns the cosine of an angle given in radians. |
| `COSH(number)` | Returns the hyperbolic cosine of a number. |
| `COT(number)` | Returns the cotangent of an angle given in radians. |
| `COTH(number)` | Returns the hyperbolic cotangent of a number. |
| `CSC(number)` | Returns the cosecant of an angle given in radians. |
| `CSCH(number)` | Returns the hyperbolic cosecant of an angle given in radians. |
| `DECIMAL(text, radix)` | Converts a text representation of a number in a given base into a decimal number. |
| `DEGREES(angle)` | Converts radians into degrees. |
| `EVEN(number)` | Rounds a number away from zero to the nearest even integer. |
| `EXP(number)` | Returns e raised to the power of a number. |
| `FACT(number)` | Returns the factorial of a number. |
| `FACTDOUBLE(number)` | Returns the double factorial of a number. |
| `FLOOR.MATH(number, [significance], [mode])` | Rounds a number down to the nearest integer or multiple of significance. |
| `FLOOR.PRECISE(number, [significance])` | Rounds a number down to the nearest multiple of significance, regardless of sign. |
| `GCD(number1, [number2], ...)` | Returns the greatest common divisor of integers. |
| `INT(number)` | Rounds a number down to the nearest integer. |
| `ISO.CEILING(number, [significance])` | Rounds a number up to the nearest multiple of significance, regardless of sign (ISO 8601 behaviour). |
| `LCM(number1, [number2], ...)` | Returns the least common multiple of integers. |
| `LN(number)` | Returns the natural logarithm of a number. |
| `LOG(number, [base])` | Returns the logarithm of a number to the base you specify. |
| `LOG10(number)` | Returns the base-10 logarithm of a number. |
| `MDETERM(array)` | Returns the matrix determinant of an array. |
| `MINVERSE(array)` | Returns the inverse matrix of a square array. |
| `MMULT(array1, array2)` | Returns the matrix product of two arrays. |
| `MOD(number, divisor)` | Returns the remainder after division; the result has the sign of the divisor. |
| `MROUND(number, multiple)` | Returns a number rounded to the nearest multiple. |
| `MULTINOMIAL(number1, [number2], ...)` | Returns the multinomial of a set of numbers. |
| `MUNIT(dimension)` | Returns the unit (identity) matrix of a given size. |
| `ODD(number)` | Rounds a number away from zero to the nearest odd integer. |
| `PERCENTOF(data_subset, data_all)` | Returns the percentage that a subset makes up of a data set: the sum of the subset divided by the sum of all the data. |
| `PI()` | Returns the value of pi, accurate to 15 digits. |
| `POWER(number, power)` | Returns the result of a number raised to a power. |
| `PRODUCT(number1, [number2], ...)` | Multiplies all the numbers given as arguments. |
| `QUOTIENT(numerator, denominator)` | Returns the integer portion of a division. |
| `RADIANS(angle)` | Converts degrees to radians. |
| `RAND()` | Returns a random number greater than or equal to 0 and less than 1 (recalculates every time). |
| `RANDARRAY([rows], [columns], [min], [max], [whole_number])` | Returns an array of random numbers. |
| `RANDBETWEEN(bottom, top)` | Returns a random integer between the numbers you specify. |
| `ROMAN(number, [form])` | Converts an Arabic numeral to Roman, as text. |
| `ROUND(number, num_digits)` | Rounds a number to a given number of digits (halves away from zero). |
| `ROUNDDOWN(number, num_digits)` | Rounds a number down, toward zero. |
| `ROUNDUP(number, num_digits)` | Rounds a number up, away from zero. |
| `SEC(number)` | Returns the secant of an angle given in radians. |
| `SECH(number)` | Returns the hyperbolic secant of an angle. |
| `SEQUENCE(rows, [columns], [start], [step])` | Generates a list of sequential numbers in an array. |
| `SERIESSUM(x, n, m, coefficients)` | Returns the sum of a power series. |
| `SIGN(number)` | Returns the sign of a number: 1, 0 or -1. |
| `SIN(number)` | Returns the sine of an angle given in radians. |
| `SINH(number)` | Returns the hyperbolic sine of a number. |
| `SQRT(number)` | Returns a positive square root. |
| `SQRTPI(number)` | Returns the square root of (number * pi). |
| `SUBTOTAL(function_num, ref1, [ref2], ...)` | Returns a subtotal in a list, ignoring other SUBTOTAL results and (for 101–111) hidden rows. |
| `SUM(number1, [number2], ...)` | Adds numbers. |
| `SUMIF(range, criteria, [sum_range])` | Adds the cells that meet a criterion. |
| `SUMIFS(sum_range, criteria_range1, criteria1, [criteria_range2, criteria2], ...)` | Adds the cells that meet several criteria. |
| `SUMPRODUCT(array1, [array2], ...)` | Returns the sum of the products of corresponding array elements. |
| `SUMSQ(number1, [number2], ...)` | Returns the sum of the squares of the arguments. |
| `SUMX2MY2(array_x, array_y)` | Returns the sum of the difference of squares of corresponding values in two arrays. |
| `SUMX2PY2(array_x, array_y)` | Returns the sum of the sum of squares of corresponding values in two arrays. |
| `SUMXMY2(array_x, array_y)` | Returns the sum of squares of differences of corresponding values in two arrays. |
| `TAN(number)` | Returns the tangent of an angle given in radians. |
| `TANH(number)` | Returns the hyperbolic tangent of a number. |
| `TRUNC(number, [num_digits])` | Truncates a number to an integer (or to the given precision). |

## Statistical

| Function | What it does |
|---|---|
| `AVEDEV(number1, [number2], ...)` | Returns the average of the absolute deviations of data points from their mean. |
| `AVERAGE(number1, [number2], ...)` | Returns the arithmetic mean of its arguments. |
| `AVERAGEA(value1, [value2], ...)` | Returns the average of its arguments, counting text in ranges as 0 and logicals as 1 or 0. |
| `AVERAGEIF(range, criteria, [average_range])` | Returns the average of the cells that meet a criterion. |
| `AVERAGEIFS(average_range, criteria_range1, criteria1, [criteria_range2, criteria2], ...)` | Returns the average of the cells that meet several criteria. |
| `BETA.DIST(x, alpha, beta, cumulative, [A], [B])` | Returns the beta distribution. |
| `BETA.INV(probability, alpha, beta, [A], [B])` | Returns the inverse of the cumulative beta distribution. |
| `BINOM.DIST(number_s, trials, probability_s, cumulative)` | Returns the individual term binomial distribution probability. |
| `BINOM.DIST.RANGE(trials, probability_s, number_s, [number_s2])` | Returns the probability of a trial result using a binomial distribution. |
| `BINOM.INV(trials, probability_s, alpha)` | Returns the smallest value for which the cumulative binomial distribution is greater than or equal to a criterion value. |
| `CHISQ.DIST(x, deg_freedom, cumulative)` | Returns the chi-squared distribution. |
| `CHISQ.DIST.RT(x, deg_freedom)` | Returns the right-tailed probability of the chi-squared distribution. |
| `CHISQ.INV(probability, deg_freedom)` | Returns the inverse of the left-tailed probability of the chi-squared distribution. |
| `CHISQ.INV.RT(probability, deg_freedom)` | Returns the inverse of the right-tailed probability of the chi-squared distribution. |
| `CHISQ.TEST(actual_range, expected_range)` | Returns the test for independence (the chi-squared probability). |
| `CONFIDENCE.NORM(alpha, standard_dev, size)` | Returns the confidence interval half-width for a population mean, using a normal distribution. |
| `CONFIDENCE.T(alpha, standard_dev, size)` | Returns the confidence interval half-width for a population mean, using a Student's t distribution. |
| `CORREL(array1, array2)` | Returns the correlation coefficient of two data sets. |
| `COUNT(value1, [value2], ...)` | Counts the cells that contain numbers. |
| `COUNTA(value1, [value2], ...)` | Counts the cells that are not empty. |
| `COUNTBLANK(range)` | Counts the empty cells in a range (cells with "" count too). |
| `COUNTIF(range, criteria)` | Counts the cells that meet a criterion. |
| `COUNTIFS(criteria_range1, criteria1, [criteria_range2, criteria2], ...)` | Counts the cells that meet several criteria. |
| `COVARIANCE.P(array1, array2)` | Returns population covariance, the average of the products of paired deviations. |
| `COVARIANCE.S(array1, array2)` | Returns the sample covariance. |
| `DEVSQ(number1, [number2], ...)` | Returns the sum of squares of deviations from the sample mean. |
| `EXPON.DIST(x, lambda, cumulative)` | Returns the exponential distribution. |
| `F.DIST(x, deg_freedom1, deg_freedom2, cumulative)` | Returns the F probability distribution. |
| `F.DIST.RT(x, deg_freedom1, deg_freedom2)` | Returns the right-tailed F probability distribution. |
| `F.INV(probability, deg_freedom1, deg_freedom2)` | Returns the inverse of the F probability distribution. |
| `F.INV.RT(probability, deg_freedom1, deg_freedom2)` | Returns the inverse of the right-tailed F probability distribution. |
| `F.TEST(array1, array2)` | Returns the result of an F-test: the two-tailed probability that the variances are not significantly different. |
| `FISHER(x)` | Returns the Fisher transformation. |
| `FISHERINV(y)` | Returns the inverse of the Fisher transformation. |
| `FORECAST.ETS(target_date, values, timeline, [seasonality], [data_completion], [aggregation])` | Predicts a future value with additive triple exponential smoothing (the AAA version of ETS). |
| `FORECAST.ETS.CONFINT(target_date, values, timeline, [confidence_level], [seasonality], [data_completion], [aggregation])` | Returns the half-width of the prediction interval of an ETS forecast at a target date. |
| `FORECAST.ETS.SEASONALITY(values, timeline, [data_completion], [aggregation])` | Returns the season length FORECAST.ETS detects in a series. |
| `FORECAST.ETS.STAT(values, timeline, statistic_type, [seasonality], [data_completion], [aggregation])` | Returns a statistic of the ETS model fitted to a series. |
| `FORECAST.LINEAR(x, known_y's, known_x's)` | Predicts a value along a linear trend from existing values. |
| `FREQUENCY(data_array, bins_array)` | Counts how often values occur within ranges of values and returns a vertical array. |
| `GAMMA(number)` | Returns the gamma function value. |
| `GAMMA.DIST(x, alpha, beta, cumulative)` | Returns the gamma distribution. |
| `GAMMA.INV(probability, alpha, beta)` | Returns the inverse of the gamma cumulative distribution. |
| `GAMMALN(x)` | Returns the natural logarithm of the gamma function. |
| `GAMMALN.PRECISE(x)` | Returns the natural logarithm of the gamma function. |
| `GAUSS(z)` | Returns the probability that a standard normal value falls between the mean and z standard deviations from it. |
| `GEOMEAN(number1, [number2], ...)` | Returns the geometric mean. |
| `GROWTH(known_y's, [known_x's], [new_x's], [const])` | Returns values along an exponential trend. |
| `HARMEAN(number1, [number2], ...)` | Returns the harmonic mean. |
| `HYPGEOM.DIST(sample_s, number_sample, population_s, number_pop, cumulative)` | Returns the hypergeometric distribution. |
| `INTERCEPT(known_y's, known_x's)` | Returns the intercept of the linear regression line. |
| `KURT(number1, [number2], ...)` | Returns the kurtosis of a data set. |
| `LARGE(array, k)` | Returns the k-th largest value in a data set. |
| `LINEST(known_y's, [known_x's], [const], [stats])` | Returns the parameters of a linear trend (and optionally regression statistics). |
| `LOGEST(known_y's, [known_x's], [const], [stats])` | Returns the parameters of an exponential trend. |
| `LOGNORM.DIST(x, mean, standard_dev, cumulative)` | Returns the lognormal distribution of x. |
| `LOGNORM.INV(probability, mean, standard_dev)` | Returns the inverse of the lognormal cumulative distribution. |
| `MAX(number1, [number2], ...)` | Returns the largest number in a set of values. |
| `MAXA(value1, [value2], ...)` | Returns the largest value, counting logicals and text in ranges. |
| `MAXIFS(max_range, criteria_range1, criteria1, [criteria_range2, criteria2], ...)` | Returns the largest value among cells that meet criteria. |
| `MEDIAN(number1, [number2], ...)` | Returns the median of the given numbers. |
| `MIN(number1, [number2], ...)` | Returns the smallest number in a set of values. |
| `MINA(value1, [value2], ...)` | Returns the smallest value, counting logicals and text in ranges. |
| `MINIFS(min_range, criteria_range1, criteria1, [criteria_range2, criteria2], ...)` | Returns the smallest value among cells that meet criteria. |
| `MODE.MULT(number1, [number2], ...)` | Returns a vertical array of the most frequently occurring values. |
| `MODE.SNGL(number1, [number2], ...)` | Returns the most frequently occurring value. |
| `NEGBINOM.DIST(number_f, number_s, probability_s, cumulative)` | Returns the negative binomial distribution. |
| `NORM.DIST(x, mean, standard_dev, cumulative)` | Returns the normal distribution for a mean and standard deviation. |
| `NORM.INV(probability, mean, standard_dev)` | Returns the inverse of the normal cumulative distribution. |
| `NORM.S.DIST(z, cumulative)` | Returns the standard normal distribution (mean 0, standard deviation 1). |
| `NORM.S.INV(probability)` | Returns the inverse of the standard normal cumulative distribution. |
| `PEARSON(array1, array2)` | Returns the Pearson product moment correlation coefficient. |
| `PERCENTILE.EXC(array, k)` | Returns the k-th percentile of values, where k is in the open range 0..1. |
| `PERCENTILE.INC(array, k)` | Returns the k-th percentile of values, where k is in the range 0..1 inclusive. |
| `PERCENTRANK.EXC(array, x, [significance])` | Returns the rank of a value in a data set as a percentage (0..1, exclusive). |
| `PERCENTRANK.INC(array, x, [significance])` | Returns the rank of a value in a data set as a percentage (0..1, inclusive). |
| `PERMUT(number, number_chosen)` | Returns the number of permutations for a given number of objects. |
| `PERMUTATIONA(number, number_chosen)` | Returns the number of permutations (with repetitions) for a given number of objects. |
| `PHI(x)` | Returns the value of the density function for a standard normal distribution. |
| `POISSON.DIST(x, mean, cumulative)` | Returns the Poisson distribution. |
| `PROB(x_range, prob_range, lower_limit, [upper_limit])` | Returns the probability that values in a range are between two limits. |
| `QUARTILE.EXC(array, quart)` | Returns the quartile of a data set, based on percentile values from 0..1, exclusive. |
| `QUARTILE.INC(array, quart)` | Returns the quartile of a data set, based on percentile values from 0..1, inclusive. |
| `RANK.AVG(number, ref, [order])` | Returns the rank of a number in a list; ties get the average rank. |
| `RANK.EQ(number, ref, [order])` | Returns the rank of a number in a list; ties get the top rank. |
| `RSQ(known_y's, known_x's)` | Returns the square of the Pearson correlation coefficient. |
| `SKEW(number1, [number2], ...)` | Returns the skewness of a distribution. |
| `SKEW.P(number1, [number2], ...)` | Returns the skewness of a distribution based on a population. |
| `SLOPE(known_y's, known_x's)` | Returns the slope of the linear regression line. |
| `SMALL(array, k)` | Returns the k-th smallest value in a data set. |
| `STANDARDIZE(x, mean, standard_dev)` | Returns a normalised value from a distribution with the given mean and standard deviation. |
| `STDEV.P(number1, [number2], ...)` | Calculates the standard deviation of an entire population. |
| `STDEV.S(number1, [number2], ...)` | Estimates the standard deviation of a sample. |
| `STDEVA(value1, [value2], ...)` | Estimates standard deviation from a sample, counting text and logicals. |
| `STDEVPA(value1, [value2], ...)` | Calculates the population standard deviation, counting text and logicals. |
| `STEYX(known_y's, known_x's)` | Returns the standard error of the predicted y-value for each x in the regression. |
| `T.DIST(x, deg_freedom, cumulative)` | Returns the left-tailed Student's t-distribution. |
| `T.DIST.2T(x, deg_freedom)` | Returns the two-tailed Student's t-distribution. |
| `T.DIST.RT(x, deg_freedom)` | Returns the right-tailed Student's t-distribution. |
| `T.INV(probability, deg_freedom)` | Returns the left-tailed inverse of the Student's t-distribution. |
| `T.INV.2T(probability, deg_freedom)` | Returns the two-tailed inverse of the Student's t-distribution. |
| `T.TEST(array1, array2, tails, type)` | Returns the probability associated with a Student's t-test. |
| `TREND(known_y's, [known_x's], [new_x's], [const])` | Returns values along a linear trend. |
| `TRIMMEAN(array, percent)` | Returns the mean of the interior of a data set, excluding a percentage of points from the top and bottom. |
| `VAR.P(number1, [number2], ...)` | Calculates variance based on the entire population. |
| `VAR.S(number1, [number2], ...)` | Estimates variance based on a sample. |
| `VARA(value1, [value2], ...)` | Estimates variance from a sample, counting text and logicals. |
| `VARPA(value1, [value2], ...)` | Calculates variance of an entire population, counting text and logicals. |
| `WEIBULL.DIST(x, alpha, beta, cumulative)` | Returns the Weibull distribution. |
| `Z.TEST(array, x, [sigma])` | Returns the one-tailed probability-value of a z-test. |

## Text

| Function | What it does |
|---|---|
| `ARRAYTOTEXT(array, [format])` | Returns an array of values as text. |
| `ASC(text)` | Changes full-width (double-byte) letters, digits and katakana to their half-width (single-byte) forms. |
| `BAHTTEXT(number)` | Converts a number to Thai text and adds the suffix "Baht". |
| `CHAR(number)` | Returns the character for a code number (Windows-1252). |
| `CLEAN(text)` | Removes non-printable characters (codes 0–31) from text. |
| `CODE(text)` | Returns the code number of the first character in text (Windows-1252). |
| `CONCAT(text1, [text2], ...)` | Joins text from several values and ranges. |
| `CONCATENATE(text1, [text2], ...)` | Joins several text strings into one. |
| `DBCS(text)` | Changes half-width (single-byte) letters, digits and katakana to their full-width (double-byte) forms. |
| `DOLLAR(number, [decimals])` | Converts a number to text in currency format. |
| `EXACT(text1, text2)` | Checks whether two text strings are exactly the same (case-sensitive). |
| `FIND(find_text, within_text, [start_num])` | Finds one text string within another (case-sensitive) and returns its position. |
| `FINDB(find_text, within_text, [start_num])` | Finds one text string within another (byte positions in double-byte languages; same as FIND otherwise). |
| `FIXED(number, [decimals], [no_commas])` | Formats a number as text with a fixed number of decimals. |
| `JIS(text)` | Changes half-width (single-byte) letters, digits and katakana to their full-width (double-byte) forms. |
| `LEFT(text, [num_chars])` | Returns the first characters of a text string. |
| `LEFTB(text, [num_bytes])` | Returns the first characters of a text string (bytes in double-byte languages). |
| `LEN(text)` | Returns the number of characters in a text string. |
| `LENB(text)` | Returns the number of bytes used to represent the text (characters in single-byte languages). |
| `LOWER(text)` | Converts text to lowercase. |
| `MID(text, start_num, num_chars)` | Returns characters from the middle of a text string. |
| `MIDB(text, start_num, num_bytes)` | Returns characters from the middle of a text string (bytes in double-byte languages). |
| `NUMBERVALUE(text, [decimal_separator], [group_separator])` | Converts text to a number in a locale-independent way. |
| `PHONETIC(reference)` | Extracts the phonetic (furigana) characters from a text string; text without furigana is returned as it is. |
| `PROPER(text)` | Capitalises the first letter of each word. |
| `REGEXEXTRACT(text, pattern, [return_mode], [case_sensitivity])` | Extracts text that matches a regular expression. |
| `REGEXREPLACE(text, pattern, replacement, [occurrence], [case_sensitivity])` | Replaces text that matches a regular expression. |
| `REGEXTEST(text, pattern, [case_sensitivity])` | Checks whether any part of text matches a regular expression. |
| `REPLACE(old_text, start_num, num_chars, new_text)` | Replaces part of a text string with different text. |
| `REPLACEB(old_text, start_num, num_bytes, new_text)` | Replaces part of a text string (bytes in double-byte languages). |
| `REPT(text, number_times)` | Repeats text a given number of times. |
| `RIGHT(text, [num_chars])` | Returns the last characters of a text string. |
| `RIGHTB(text, [num_bytes])` | Returns the last characters of a text string (bytes in double-byte languages). |
| `SEARCH(find_text, within_text, [start_num])` | Finds one text string within another (not case-sensitive, wildcards allowed) and returns its position. |
| `SEARCHB(find_text, within_text, [start_num])` | Finds one text string within another (byte positions in double-byte languages). |
| `SUBSTITUTE(text, old_text, new_text, [instance_num])` | Substitutes new text for old text in a text string. |
| `T(value)` | Returns the text referred to by a value, or "" for non-text. |
| `TEXT(value, format_text)` | Formats a number and converts it to text using a number format code. |
| `TEXTAFTER(text, delimiter, [instance_num], [match_mode], [match_end], [if_not_found])` | Returns text that occurs after a given delimiter. |
| `TEXTBEFORE(text, delimiter, [instance_num], [match_mode], [match_end], [if_not_found])` | Returns text that occurs before a given delimiter. |
| `TEXTJOIN(delimiter, ignore_empty, text1, [text2], ...)` | Joins text with a delimiter, optionally skipping empty values. |
| `TEXTSPLIT(text, col_delimiter, [row_delimiter], [ignore_empty], [match_mode], [pad_with])` | Splits text into rows and columns using delimiters. |
| `TRIM(text)` | Removes extra spaces from text, leaving single spaces between words. |
| `UNICHAR(number)` | Returns the Unicode character for a code point. |
| `UNICODE(text)` | Returns the Unicode code point of the first character of text. |
| `UPPER(text)` | Converts text to uppercase. |
| `VALUE(text)` | Converts a text string that represents a number (or date or time) to a number. |
| `VALUETOTEXT(value, [format])` | Returns text from any value. |

## Web

| Function | What it does |
|---|---|
| `ENCODEURL(text)` | Returns a URL-encoded (percent-encoded) string. |
